states.name: Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu

festivals.name: Ugadi
festivals.description: Homes are decorated with mango leaves and families share ugadi pachadi, whose contrasting flavours symbolise the experiences of life.

festivals.name: Sankranti
festivals.description: Rangoli, decorated cattle and family gatherings mark the harvest season.

festivals.name: Dree
festivals.description: The Apatani community gathers for agricultural rituals, songs and dances, offering prayers for a healthy crop.

festivals.name: Losar
festivals.description: Monpa communities welcome the new year with monastery prayers, family visits and traditional food.

festivals.name: Bohag Bihu
festivals.description: Also called Rongali Bihu, this spring celebration welcomes the Assamese New Year with Bihu dance, music and festive meals.
festivals.story: Bohag, or Rongali, Bihu marks the Assamese New Year and the arrival of the agricultural spring. It is distinct from Magh Bihu after the harvest and Kati Bihu later in the farming cycle.
rituals: Family visits and exchanges of gamosa cloths
festivals.food: Pitha and laru are familiar festive foods; recipes differ between communities.
festivals.dress: Mekhela chador and gamosa are associated with Assamese celebrations.
tips: Seek a publicly advertised performance if you are visiting independently.
Ask before entering a household celebration.
places: Public Bihu stages and cultural programmes.

festivals.name: Magh Bihu
festivals.description: Community feasts and ceremonial meji bonfires celebrate the end of the harvest season.

festivals.name: Chhath Puja
festivals.description: Devotees offer prayers to the setting and rising sun at rivers and ponds, with fasting and carefully prepared offerings.
festivals.story: Chhath is an observance of gratitude to the sun and Chhathi Maiya. It is especially associated with Bihar and neighbouring regions, and is also observed by communities far from their home states.
festivals.food: Thekua and fruit are among the offerings; preparation follows household religious practices.
festivals.dress: Dress respectfully and keep worship areas clear.
tips: Do not interrupt fasting devotees or step across offerings.
Stay behind waterside barriers; ask before close-up photographs.
places: Designated river ghats; access arrangements change by year.

festivals.name: Sonepur Mela
festivals.description: Around Kartik Purnima, pilgrims, performers and traders gather at this historic riverside fair.

festivals.name: Bastar Dussehra
festivals.description: A long cycle of rituals honours Goddess Danteshwari, bringing together local communities, ceremonial chariots and regional deities.

festivals.name: Hareli
festivals.description: Farming communities honour agricultural tools and celebrate the green season with local games and traditions.

festivals.name: Carnival
festivals.description: Colourful floats, music and dancing fill the streets in the days leading up to Lent.

festivals.name: Shigmo
festivals.description: Folk dances, processions and elaborate floats bring Goan spring traditions into public celebrations.

festivals.name: Navratri
festivals.description: Nine nights of devotion to the goddess are celebrated with circular garba dancing and dandiya raas.
festivals.story: Navratri honours the goddess over nine nights. Gujarat's garba circles and dandiya gatherings are especially well known, while other regions have distinct devotional and artistic traditions. This guide focuses on the autumn celebration.
festivals.food: Fasting and festive menus differ. Ask hosts about the customs of the event you attend.
festivals.dress: Chaniya cholis and kediyu outfits are associated with Gujarati celebrations; comfortable footwear and freedom of movement matter.
tips: Join dancing only where visitors are welcome; follow the direction of the circle.
Check passes and entry rules for each venue.
places: Large organised dance gatherings; passes vary.

festivals.name: Uttarayan
festivals.description: Rooftops fill with kite flyers during Makar Sankranti, with festive food and colourful skies.

festivals.name: Teej
festivals.description: Songs, swings and gatherings celebrate the arrival of the monsoon and the traditions of Teej.

festivals.name: Surajkund International Crafts Mela
festivals.description: Artisans and performers gather for a major cultural fair showcasing handicrafts, folk traditions and regional food.

festivals.name: Kullu Dussehra
festivals.description: Valley deities are brought to Kullu in a gathering centred on Lord Raghunath, with processions and cultural programmes.

festivals.name: Mandi Shivratri
festivals.description: Local deities, devotees and performers gather for a celebration associated with Maha Shivratri.

festivals.name: Sarhul
festivals.description: Several Adivasi communities honour sacred groves and the flowering sal tree with rituals, music and dancing.

festivals.name: Karam
festivals.description: Community celebrations centre on the Karam tree, with songs and dances expressing hopes for wellbeing and prosperity.

festivals.name: Mysuru Dasara
festivals.description: An illuminated palace, performances and the celebrated procession make Dasara a signature Mysuru experience.
festivals.story: Mysuru Dasara combines worship of Chamundeshwari with the city's royal and public cultural heritage. Palace illumination and performances build towards the festival's celebrated procession. Specific programmes can have separate tickets.
festivals.food: Mysore pak is a local sweet to try; it is not exclusive to Dasara.
festivals.dress: Comfortable clothing works for public viewing; follow dress requirements in religious venues.
tips: Verify procession dates and viewing arrangements separately.
Book accommodation early and allow for traffic restrictions.
places: Palace area and announced city programme locations.

festivals.name: Onam
festivals.description: Floral pookalam designs, the onasadya feast and cultural performances celebrate the homecoming of King Mahabali.
festivals.story: Onam celebrates seasonal abundance and the legendary return of King Mahabali. It brings Malayali families and communities together through floral designs, hospitality and performances. Public programmes and household traditions have different schedules.
rituals: An Onasadya meal served on a banana leaf
festivals.food: Sadya is a vegetarian feast with rice, vegetable dishes and payasam; menus vary by household and venue.
festivals.dress: Kerala kasavu textiles are often worn for celebrations. Comfortable, respectful clothing is suitable for visitors.
tips: Book a public sadya rather than assuming access to a private family meal.
Boat races are separate events: verify their dates independently.
places: Look for announced city cultural programmes.
Community celebrations and public sadya meals.

photo.alt: Children performing a boat-song scene during an Onam celebration
photo.caption: Children singing vallappaattu during Onam, 2010. Historical photograph.
photo.author: Ramjchandran

festivals.name: Vishu
festivals.description: The day begins with viewing the auspicious Vishukkani arrangement, followed by gifts and family meals.

festivals.name: Bhagoria
festivals.description: Bhil and Bhilala communities gather at lively fairs before Holi, with music, dancing and market stalls.

festivals.name: Khajuraho Dance Festival
festivals.description: Indian classical dance traditions are showcased against the backdrop of Khajuraho’s temple heritage.

festivals.name: Ganesh Chaturthi
festivals.description: Ganesha idols are welcomed into homes and public pandals, with prayers, modak sweets and immersion processions.
festivals.story: Ganesh Chaturthi welcomes Ganesha into homes and public pandals. Maharashtra's community celebrations combine worship, craftsmanship and collective organisation. Household observances vary in duration, so immersion days are not identical everywhere.
festivals.food: Modak sweets are strongly associated with Ganesha; recipes and offerings vary.
festivals.dress: Respectful, comfortable clothing is suitable; follow temple or pandal instructions.
tips: Use designated viewing areas for processions and immersion.
Allow extra time for queues and temporary road closures.
places: Major public pandals and immersion routes.

festivals.name: Gudi Padwa
festivals.description: Families raise decorated gudis outside their homes to welcome the new year.

festivals.name: Yaoshang
festivals.description: A multiday spring celebration combines devotional traditions, local sports and thabal chongba dancing.

festivals.name: Sangai Festival
festivals.description: A tourism festival presents the state’s dance, crafts, food and cultural traditions.

festivals.name: Wangala
festivals.description: Garo communities celebrate the harvest with drumming and dancing, giving thanks to the sun deity.

festivals.name: Nongkrem Dance Festival
festivals.description: Khasi ceremonial traditions and dances express thanksgiving and prayers for prosperity.

festivals.name: Chapchar Kut
festivals.description: A Mizo spring festival with music, traditional dress and dances including the bamboo dance, Cheraw.

festivals.name: Mim Kut
festivals.description: A traditional maize-season observance combines remembrance of departed relatives with community customs.

festivals.name: Hornbill Festival
festivals.description: Naga communities share performances, crafts, food and traditions at a major annual cultural gathering.
festivals.story: Organised as a cultural showcase since 2000, Hornbill brings together different Naga communities. It offers performances, crafts and food alongside contemporary events. The shared programme does not replace each community's own festivals or distinct traditions.
festivals.food: Stalls offer different Naga cuisines. Ask vendors about ingredients, spice levels and vegetarian options.
festivals.dress: Community textiles and ornaments have specific meanings; ask before borrowing, handling or photographing them closely.
tips: Check the current official programme and visitor requirements before booking.
Ask performers before portraits, and keep performance areas clear.
places: Main cultural showcase near Kohima; programme and access are organiser-dependent.

photo.alt: Participant wearing traditional dress at the Hornbill Festival in Kisama
photo.caption: Hornbill Festival at Kisama, 2024. Historical photograph.
photo.author: JyotiPN

festivals.name: Moatsu
festivals.description: After sowing, Ao communities celebrate with songs, dances and communal gatherings.

festivals.name: Rath Yatra
festivals.description: The deities Jagannath, Balabhadra and Subhadra travel in monumental wooden chariots through Puri.
festivals.story: Puri's Rath Yatra brings Jagannath, Balabhadra and Subhadra into a public chariot procession. The journey forms part of a larger cycle of observances, including the return journey, which must be checked separately.
festivals.food: Mahaprasad is associated with Jagannath traditions; seek guidance on authorised distribution.
festivals.dress: Wear respectful clothing and practical footwear for long periods outdoors.
tips: Use authorised viewing arrangements rather than entering dense chariot crowds.
Temple entry restrictions differ from access to the public procession.
places: Grand Road procession corridor; access follows local arrangements.

festivals.name: Raja Parba
festivals.description: A celebration associated with the earth’s fertility, featuring swings, pitha and a pause in agricultural work.

festivals.name: Vaisakhi
festivals.description: Harvest celebrations coincide with the commemoration of the formation of the Khalsa, with gurdwara visits and community meals.
festivals.story: Vaisakhi brings together Punjab's harvest season and the Sikh commemoration of the formation of the Khalsa. Gurdwara visits, service and community meals are important, alongside local fairs and cultural programmes.
festivals.food: Langar is a communal meal grounded in service and equality; follow the volunteers' guidance.
festivals.dress: Cover your head and remove shoes where required in a gurdwara.
tips: Ask about visitor procedures at each religious venue.
Keep paths clear and ask before photographing worshippers.
places: Local Vaisakhi fair and religious celebrations.

festivals.name: Lohri
festivals.description: Families and communities gather around bonfires with folk songs and seasonal foods.

festivals.name: Gangaur
festivals.description: Women honour Gauri with rituals, decorated images and colourful processions.
festivals.story: Gangaur honours Gauri and is especially associated with women's devotional traditions in Rajasthan. Udaipur's Mewar Festival overlaps with these celebrations, giving the occasion a distinctive lakeside expression.
festivals.food: Seek regional sweets and seasonal dishes; customs vary between families and towns.
festivals.dress: Colourful saris and regional dress are common in processions.
tips: Photograph respectfully without blocking processions.
Check the local route rather than assuming all cities share one programme.
places: Gangaur traditions around the old city and lakeside.
City processions subject to annual announcements.

festivals.name: Pushkar Fair
festivals.description: Around Kartik Purnima, pilgrims and visitors gather for a traditional fair, cultural events and lakeside rituals.

festivals.name: Losoong / Namsoong
festivals.description: Bhutia and Lepcha communities mark seasonal renewal through their distinct traditions and celebrations.

festivals.name: Pongal
festivals.description: Families prepare freshly harvested rice in a ceremonial pot and honour the sun and cattle over several days.
festivals.story: Pongal expresses gratitude for the harvest, the sun and the animals that support farming. The festival unfolds through several days with different meanings, connecting Tamil households to the agricultural season.
rituals: Cooking freshly harvested rice until the pot overflows
festivals.food: Sweet sakkarai pongal is made with rice and jaggery; other dishes vary by household.
festivals.dress: Saris and veshtis are common festive clothing, though there is no universal visitor dress requirement.
tips: Ask permission before joining household or village ceremonies.
Treat animal-related events as separate programmes with their own access rules.
places: Tamil harvest traditions in and around the city.

festivals.name: Tamil Puthandu
festivals.description: Temple visits, festive meals and decorated entrances welcome the Tamil New Year.

festivals.name: Bathukamma
festivals.description: Women arrange seasonal flowers in tiered stacks and gather around them to sing and celebrate.
festivals.story: Bathukamma celebrates seasonal flowers and the goddess through a distinctly Telangana tradition. Women arrange tiered floral stacks and gather around them to sing, before concluding celebrations at local water bodies.
rituals: Singing in circles around the flowers
festivals.food: Shared offerings vary by day; maleeda is associated with celebrations.
festivals.dress: Festive saris and regional textiles are common; observe local guidance when joining a gathering.
tips: Ask a host before joining a community circle.
Use designated viewing areas and protect the flowers and waterside space.
places: Public gatherings and neighbourhood celebrations; venues vary each year.

festivals.name: Bonalu
festivals.description: Devotees offer decorated pots of food to the goddess Mahakali, accompanied by local processions.

festivals.name: Kharchi Puja
festivals.description: The Fourteen Gods are honoured through rituals and a public fair at the Chaturdasha Devata temple.

festivals.name: Garia Puja
festivals.description: Traditional prayers and community celebrations seek wellbeing and a prosperous agricultural season.

festivals.name: Holi
festivals.description: The Braj region’s distinctive celebrations combine devotional singing and colourful traditions over several days.
festivals.story: Holi celebrates spring through colour, gathering and stories of renewal. In the Braj region, celebrations are connected with Krishna traditions. Different towns hold distinct events on different days around the main festival.
rituals: Holika Dahan bonfires in many communities
festivals.food: Gujiya is a familiar festive sweet in northern India; local menus vary.
festivals.dress: Choose comfortable clothes that can be stained. Clothing is not consent to participate.
tips: Ask before applying colour or photographing participants.
Select an organised event if you prefer clear boundaries and facilities.
places: Temple programmes require their own date and access checks.

festivals.name: Dev Deepawali
festivals.description: On Kartik Purnima, thousands of lamps illuminate the Ganges ghats in a spectacular riverside celebration.

festivals.name: Harela
festivals.description: Seedlings grown in the days before the festival symbolise greenery, prosperity and the agricultural season.

festivals.name: Phool Dei
festivals.description: Children place flowers at doorsteps to welcome spring and offer blessings for the household.

festivals.name: Durga Puja
festivals.description: Neighbourhoods become open-air galleries of elaborate pandals and Durga idols. Dhak drums, dhunuchi dance and shared bhog bring people together in a celebration of creativity and devotion.
festivals.story: Durga Puja honours the goddess Durga and her victory over Mahishasura. In Bengal, it is also imagined as a daughter's homecoming. Kolkata's neighbourhood pandals make the celebration a meeting of public art, craftsmanship and worship.
rituals: Pandal visits and viewing crafted idols
Dhak drumming, prayers and dhunuchi dance
Immersion processions at the close of the observance
festivals.food: Shared bhog often includes khichuri; sweets and family meals are part of the wider celebrations.
festivals.dress: Saris, kurtas and everyday festive clothing; red-and-white combinations are a familiar sight, not a visitor requirement.
tips: Ask before photographing worship or individuals.
Visit earlier in the day for a gentler introduction; evening queues can be long.
places: Neighbourhood pandals and public art; individual opening times vary.

photo.alt: Durga idol and accompanying figures inside an illuminated pandal in West Bengal
photo.caption: Durga Puja in West Bengal, 2022. Historical photograph; not a preview of the current year's event.
photo.author: Prantik006

festivals.name: Kali Puja
festivals.description: Homes and temples honour Goddess Kali with lamps, offerings and evening worship around the new moon.

festivals.name: Poila Boishakh
festivals.description: New account books, cultural programmes and generous Bengali meals mark the start of the Bengali year.

festivals.name: Island Tourism Festival
festivals.description: A public cultural programme showcases island communities through performances, exhibitions and local food; confirm the organiser’s current schedule.

festivals.name: Rose Festival
festivals.description: Flower displays and cultural activities celebrate the city’s garden heritage.

festivals.name: Nariyal Purnima
festivals.description: Fishing communities offer coconuts to the sea, accompanied by prayers and local celebrations.

festivals.name: Diwali
festivals.description: Diyas, family gatherings, sweets and worship mark the festival of lights in the capital.

festivals.name: Eid al-Fitr
festivals.description: Prayers, charitable giving and festive meals mark the end of Ramadan; dates depend on the lunar calendar.

festivals.name: Herath
festivals.description: The Kashmiri observance of Shivratri centres on family worship, ritual offerings and festive food.

festivals.name: Hemis Festival
festivals.description: Masked cham dances and monastery rituals commemorate Guru Padmasambhava.
festivals.story: Hemis Festival honours Guru Padmasambhava at Hemis Monastery in Ladakh. Its cham dances are religious performances, not simply entertainment. The annual dates follow the Tibetan lunar calendar.
festivals.food: Explore local Ladakhi food outside the ritual spaces; follow monastery rules on eating.
festivals.dress: Modest layers suit monastery visits and changeable mountain conditions.
tips: Ask before photographing religious performances or interiors.
Confirm seating and step-free access with the monastery or organiser.
places: Monastery courtyard; visitor arrangements depend on the programme.

events.place: India-wide observance; local Braj events vary
events.note: Main holiday date, not the full Braj programme.
Opening observance only. Household durations and immersion dates vary.
Autumn Navratri listing. Individual garba venues set their own schedules and tickets.
Tourism listing extends to 21 October; it is not a confirmed procession date. Verify the local programme before booking.
Tourism listing shows 17–21 October; local ritual calendars may differ. Verify with the pandal organiser.
Main listed observance, not every regional or multiday celebration.
